elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" — "for any reason" is a convenience right, and with "following the Initial Term" deleted and the Initial Term bar narrowed to Kubient, AP may exercise it at any time. The Agreement uses no Order Form construct, so Agreement-level termination suffices. (The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a regex false negative: the right is expressed as "Either Party ... for any reason" rather than "Customer ... for convenience".)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The retained notice period is "ninety (90) days written notice"; no 30-day Customer notice was inserted. To reach preferred, the drafter would need a separate sentence giving Customer a 30-day convenience notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language exists anywhere in the rendered text; the only money sentence runs the other way ("Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period"). A pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation would have to be added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may not terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit" plus "any termination by Kubient under this sentence shall be effective only at the end of the then-current Term" bar Kubient from exiting mid-Initial-Term or mid-renewal-term. Residual note: the retained "or any Exhibit" carve-out now benefits only Kubient and could in principle host a mid-term Kubient exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" — 90 days is within the 60–90 band, and the Initial Term lock-in now binds only Kubient ("Kubient may not terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term"), so AP's right is unrestricted as to timing.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No penalty or early-termination fee is imposed on Customer. The retained sentence gives Kubient only "all fees generated during the termination period" — i.e. revenue-share fees actually earned through the 90-day notice window, which cannot exceed three months of fees on an AP-initiated exit. Condition is therefore inapplicable, so the element is satisfied; note the phrase "termination period" is undefined, and a clarifying tie to the 90-day notice window would remove any argument that it reaches the balance of the Term.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Added proviso: "provided that any termination by Kubient under this sentence shall be effective only at the end of the then-current Term" — the effective date is expressly anchored to term-end, satisfying the rule that an auto-renewal notice right is not term-end-only unless so anchored.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The mutual notice requirement is retained verbatim — "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" — and binds Kubient equally.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day mutual notice retained, AP lock-in removed, Kubient lock-in retained, Kubient exit anchored to end of then-current Term, no early-termination penalty).

Preferred is not reached (90-day rather than 30-day Customer notice; no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund), which is consistent with the claimed fallback target and with a revenue-share structure carrying no prepaid fees.

Minimality holds: three surgical changes — "Neither Party" narrowed to "Kubient", deletion of "following the Initial Term", and the term-end proviso — each traceable to fallback elements 1 and 3. The auto-renewal mechanic, 4(b) breach/insolvency rights, the Exhibit carve-out and the Kubient fee-entitlement sentence are all retained; no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures were added.

Intent preserved: no undefined term is introduced, no cross-reference dangles, and the retained sentences do not contradict the edit — Kubient's convenience right sits under both the Initial Term bar and the term-end proviso, and AP's right is unqualified.

Deterministic signal check: "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical false negative; the right is drafted as "Either Party may terminate ... for any reason", which in substance is a Customer convenience right with no timing restriction after the edit.

Optional hardening (not required for completeness): (i) define "termination period" as the 90-day notice period so Kubient's fee entitlement cannot be read to reach the balance of the Term, and (ii) consider deleting or qualifying the retained "or any Exhibit" exception, which after the edit operates solely as a Kubient escape from the Initial Term bar.
